Gas Production and Monetization In the third quarter, future gas growth out of the Permian Basin received significant attention as a WhiteWater-led consortium (that includes Diamondback) reached Final Investment Decision (“FID”) on another large diameter pipeline out of the basin. This pipe is called Solitude and is set to enter service in the second half of 2029. This project consists of two twin 48" lines able to move 4.5 bcf/d out of the Permian to Katy and Gulf Coast markets, with potential to expand to 7.5 bcf/d. While the market was surprised that another pipe reached FID this quickly after multiple announcements over the last 18 months, we were not. As we have said many times, the Permian Basin has not tried to produce gas yet. We expect the Permian to be the largest natural gas play as well as the largest oil play in the United States in the 2030s. Gas to oil ratios will naturally continue to expand, secondary zones in both the Midland and the Delaware Basins are gassier than what operators have targeted to date and there are gas-weighted exploratory zones that have not even been tested yet given the perpetual egress issues out of this basin. As for Diamondback’s strategy, our goal is to continue to control more of our gas further downstream to a mix of end markets, primarily feeding the Gulf Coast LNG complex.
